problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=(3t-6){e}^{-t},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.

The acceleration is zero at $t=$
{{field-1}}, and the velocity at this moment is
$v=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((3t-6){e}^{-t}) \\  & =3{e}^{-t}+(3t-6)(-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =(9-3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((9-3t){e}^{-t}) \\  & =(-3){e}^{-t}+(9-3t)(-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =(3t-12){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3t-12){e}^{-t} & =0 \\ 3t-12 & =0 \\ t & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=4.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(4)=(9-3\cdot 4){e}^{-4}=-3{e}^{-4}.
$$

Therefore, the acceleration is zero at $t=4,$ and the velocity at this moment is $v=-3{e}^{-4}.$
